cands.bio: Republican state senator for Alabama District 3 (Morgan, Madison and Limestone counties) since 2006. Attorney and Executive Vice President at Cook's Pest Control. Former Peace Corps volunteer in Nepal and Habitat for Humanity attorney in Asia. Chairs the Senate Finance and Taxation Education Committee.
cands.gaps: We found no documented actions or stated positions from Orr on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, H-1B or immigration enforcement, donor money, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no public statements by him for or against data centers or more development. We found no documented controversies. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2026. The copy of his official website we had was cut off partway through the About page, so we did not use anything past that point. Wikipedia mentions a 2016 bill he sponsored on Israel boycotts. We did not read the bill itself and did not count it as foreign ties.

cands.bio: John Dickey, PhD, is a Democrat who ran for Alabama State Senate District 3 in 2026. His campaign site says he holds a political science doctorate from the University of Tennessee and has worked cattle and taught students of all ages.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended by the voter guides Tabitha's List (Sway group by Tabitha Isner) and Unburdening The Ballot (Sway group by Tevin Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find John Dickey's birthplace, hometown, or the year he moved to Alabama, only that he says he has lived in the Tennessee Valley all his life. We found no record of elected office, and no details of his teaching jobs or employers. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no documented actions in office, no stated positions on homestead taxes, investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, policing, abortion or school choice, and no news coverage or controversies about him.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he has called the Tennessee Valley home all his life and that his father is a farmer who raised him, but it gives no birthplace and does not name the state or town where he grew up.

score.why: Raised $949, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Campaign site says he has worked cattle, taught all age ranges, and earned a doctorate in Political Science from the University of Tennessee. No elected office or legislative, policy or budget career is documented.
qual.why: Teaching and a political science doctorate are relevant but are not a legislative, policy or budget career, and no prior office is shown. Details of his teaching jobs and employers were not found, so the score sits in the low-middle range.
qual.label: Teaching and a political science doctorate are relevant but are not a legislative, policy or budget career, and no prior office is shown. Details of his teaching jobs and employers were not found, so the score sits in the low-middle range.

stop-data-centers.evidence: His campaign site calls for a moratorium on data center construction and says the PSC, the Attorney General and local governments should have the tools to regulate data centers, including telling companies "no" in communities that don't want them.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he would ban Flock cameras. Nothing was found on his stance on red-flag laws, suppressors or purchase ages.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site pledges to repeal SB231 and protect card check, and to support a state minimum wage. These are labor positions, not statements on immigration enforcement or H-1B, so they only loosely bear on this plank.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: His campaign site says he has called the Tennessee Valley home all his life and that his father is a farmer who raised him, but it gives no birthplace and does not name the state or town where he grew up.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign issues page calls for a moratorium on data center construction, for data centers to pay their entire cost of operating in Alabama, for ending NDAs between businesses and local officials, and for letting local governments say "no" to data centers in communities that don't want them.
